chunks: And from him, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
A single Iqamah suffices for you in the prayer, except for the morning (Fajr) and the evening (Maghrib) prayers.

key_terms.إِقَامَةٌ: Iqamah (the second call to prayer, preceding the prayer)
key_terms.وَالْمَغْرِبَ: And the evening (referring to Maghrib prayer)

ai.seo_question: How many Iqamahs are required for Fajr and Maghrib prayers according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the procedural requirement for the Iqamah, establishing that while a single recitation suffices for most prayers, the Fajr and Maghrib prayers necessitate two Iqamahs. This distinction highlights the specific ritual emphasis placed on the dawn and evening prayers within Shia jurisprudence, often linked to their unique spiritual significance and the timing of the Adhan. The ruling underscores the meticulous attention to detail in the performance of Salah, ensuring the congregational or individual prayer is properly preceded by the necessary calls.
